transcript:
Header: Redwood All-Hands - May 27 2026
Start time: 10:00 AM PT | Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Leadership + company (approx 150)
Recording note: Live captions used; minor speaker mislabels likely.

[00:00] Aisha: Hey everyone, good morning, good afternoon, welcome to the May all-hands. We're gonna run for about an hour, we've got a packed agenda, and I'm gonna hand it over to Carlos to kick off with infra and perf.

[00:25] Carlos: Thanks Aisha. Quick stat first - our median L1 latency for hosted API across the curated model set is down 12% month over month, we're seeing the KV cache improvements land in prod. Quick caveat, the numbers vary a lot by seq length, so please check the perf sheet. Link in the follow-up.

[00:48] Speaker 3: Nice. Is that from the new kernel selection changes?

[00:52] Carlos: Yeah, it's a mix - kernel selection, better batching heuristics, and a small change to our continuous batching timeout. Also the smart routing change is in canary for a subset of customers, routing by latency vs cost. We still have edge cases where fallback to smaller quantized variants increases variance, we're tracking those.

[01:20] Jon: Adding on, infra team deployed a rollout for Dedicated autoscale tuning last week - initial customers saw improved tail latency under burst. There's a POC with a large fintech customer where we saw CPU-bound pre-processing causing a few seconds of jitter, we debugged at their side, but overall good.

[01:45] Aisha: Great. Maya, product roadmap?

[01:49] Maya: Hi, thanks. High level Q2 priorities: 1) Make Redwood Optimize more prescriptive - automated batch/cache suggestions delivered as easy toggles in Console; 2) Improve Private deployment onboarding (automated VPC templates, improved KMS docs); 3) First-class evals integration so teams can tie regressions to rollouts. We're aiming to ship Optimize toggles in beta by mid-June.

[02:20] Speaker 4: When you say Private onboarding, does that include an on-prem air-gapped install?

[02:27] Maya: Yes, the plan is customers will get a hardened package and documented steps; we still expect some manual ops for air-gapped installs but the goal is to reduce that. We'll publish the KMS/HSM integration checklist as part of the package.

[02:45] Aisha: On GTM, Lena?

[02:48] Lena: Sales summary: pipeline is healthy. A few notable deals - a retail chain moving to Dedicated, a healthcare POC that needs Private with SOC2 + ISO statements. PLG motion is still our top funnel driver; self-serve signups up 18% month over month. We're tightening the qualification to accelerate handoffs to AE once usage hits Dedicated threshold.

[03:15] Speaker 5: Any updates on pricing? Customers ask about unit economics for high token usage.

[03:20] Lena: We're preparing example commit tiers for Dedicated and clearer docs on batching/quantization tradeoffs. Sales to share a pricing FAQ next week.

[03:35] Carlos: Quick note on costs - the Optimize suggestions will start with conservative batch sizes, customers can opt in to aggressive quantization profiles; we will provide expected token-cost deltas per profile in Console so people aren't surprised.

[04:02] Aisha: Hiring update?

[04:05] Jon: We're hiring infra SREs and a couple of inference engine engineers, goal to onboard by Q3. Interview funnel looks good but the top-of-funnel needs more diversity; recruiting is running a new campus program.

[04:25] Aisha: OK, customer wins?

[04:29] Lena: We closed a mid-market SaaS that used our hosted API for embeddings and is now expanding to Dedicated. They cited reliability and the roadmap as reasons. We'll publish a short case study soon.

[04:50] Maya: Also, Canary rollout tooling has been used successfully by two customers to test model upgrades with automatic fallback - that's a nice validation of rollout abstractions.

[05:05] Q&A (selected)

[05:07] Speaker 6: Is there a plan to expose more fine-grained tracing for token latency in Console?

[05:12] Carlos: Yes, perf team is working on token-level tracing hooks that can be enabled per route, but we need to balance trace volume and cost. Planned beta next quarter.

[05:30] Speaker 7: Security question - for Private deployments, can customers bring their own KMS?

[05:35] Maya: Yes, BYOK is supported for Private, and the upcoming docs include how to wire in AWS KMS and common HSM flows. For air-gapped installs, we document the manual key provisioning steps.

[05:55] Speaker 8: Are we seeing any churn signals related to pricing?

[06:00] Lena: Churn is low. Most pricing pushback comes from large token-volume customers; our focus is to surface Optimize recommendations and trusted benchmarking so they can quantify savings.

[06:20] Mike (Sales engineer): We should also provide more sample Jupyter notebooks for benchmarking Dedicated vs hosted - customers ask for side-by-side throughput/cost scripts.

[06:32] Aisha: Good idea, Mike - Jon, can we add that to infra deliverables?

[06:36] Jon: Yep, we'll add a repo with benchmarking scripts and a spreadsheet template.

[06:50] Cross-talk and micro-discussion about internal offsite planning, skipped here for time.

[07:05] Closing remarks Aisha: Quick recap - product to ship Optimize toggles beta mid-June, infra to share benchmark notes, sales to update pricing FAQ, recruiting ramping. We want everyone to be able to point to one tangible impact this quarter. Thank you.

[07:30] Final: Links mentioned - Q2 roadmap deck (link forthcoming), perf benchmark sheet (link forthcoming), Dedicated pricing FAQ (link forthcoming). Recording and slides will be posted in #all-hands.

End of transcript.
